# Overlapping bar graphs {#sec-overlapping-bar-graphs}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()

ggplot2::theme_set(ggrewindr::theme_netware(

```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_netware()`

Graphs in this chapter use `ggrewindr::theme_netware()`, built from Novell NetWare 2.0 boxes: a NetWare red background with white text, a maroon frame, maroon, red, rose, and blush marks, and a Cabin title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

::: {.fm-req-title}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {.fm-req}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**

**✅ a categorical variable** 
:::

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1990)
netware_offices <- tibble(
  year = c("1990", "1994", "1998"),
  mean_nodes = c(22, 24, 27)) |>
  tidyr::uncount(24, .id = "office") |>
  mutate(nodes = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_nodes, sd = 2.5)),
         lan_size = if_else(nodes >= 25, "25 or more", "Under 25")) |>
  select(year, office, nodes, lan_size)
labs_bar_ovrlp <- labs(
  title = "Novell NetWare",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "Workstations per office LAN in three years",
  x = "Workstations",
  y = "Offices",
  fill = "Year")
ggp2_bar_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_offices,
          aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) +
                geom_bar(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5)
ggp2_bar_ovrlp + 
  labs_bar_ovrlp
```

::::

## Description

Overlapping bar graphs show several groups on the same graph. The bars overlap instead of sitting side by side, so we usually make them partly transparent to let the bars behind show through. A legend tells the groups apart.

In `ggplot2`, we can build overlapping bar graphs using the `fill` argument in `geom_bar()` or `geom_col()`.

## Set up

### PACKAGES {.unnumbered .fm-step}

::: {.fm-small}
Install packages.
:::


```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
library(tidyr) # for uncount()
```

### DATA {.unnumbered .fm-step}

::: {.fm-small}
Novell NetWare was the most popular network operating system of the early 90s. Office LANs grew as more desks got a PC and a network card.

We'll simulate the number of workstations on the LAN for 24 offices in 1990, 1994, and 1998. Each year gets its own average LAN size (`mean_nodes`), `tidyr::uncount()` creates one row per office, and `rnorm()` draws each office's workstation count, rounded to a whole workstation. We'll also flag whether each office ran 25 workstations or more (`lan_size`). Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 72 offices every time you run the code below.
:::

```{r}
#| label: data_code_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1990) # same 72 offices every time the code runs
netware_offices <- tibble(
  year = c("1990", "1994", "1998"), # three survey years
  mean_nodes = c(22, 24, 27) # average workstations per office (networks grow over time)
  ) |>
  tidyr::uncount(24, .id = "office") |> # 24 offices in each year
  mutate(
    nodes = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_nodes, sd = 2.5)), # each office's workstation count
    lan_size = if_else(nodes >= 25, "25 or more", "Under 25") # sort offices into two sizes
    ) |>
  select(year, office, nodes, lan_size)
glimpse(netware_offices)
```

## Distribution

Overlapping bars only overlap when groups share values. Three years with very different LAN sizes would sit side by side with no stacking at all. Three years with the same LAN size would stack into a single pile.

How much the bars overlap depends on how far apart the years' averages are compared to how much offices vary within a year. Below we'll move from the offices, to a picture, to the formula. Then we'll change the data and see what the graph does with an unexpected year.

### COUNT IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

Start with the first six offices from 1990.

```{r}
#| label: count_values_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(netware_offices, 6)
```

These offices ran between 20 and 26 workstations. The summary below shows each year's mean, standard deviation, and range.

```{r}
#| label: count_summary_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
netware_offices |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(nodes), 
    sd = sd(nodes), 
    min = min(nodes), 
    max = max(nodes))
```

In each year, the largest office runs 8 to 11 more workstations than the smallest, but the means are only about 2 to 5 workstations apart. So the ranges overlap, which is what puts more than one color in the same bar.

### DRAW IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

The overlapping bar graph below stacks the offices from all three years at each LAN size. The dashed lines mark the average LAN size we gave each year in `rnorm()`. The 1990 offices sit mostly on the left, the 1998 offices mostly on the right, and the 1994 offices land in the middle, sharing bars with both.

```{r}
#| label: draw_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(data = netware_offices, 
    aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) + 
  geom_bar() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(22, 24, 27), 
    color = c("#69100A", "#A91E28", "#B3575A"), 
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) + 
  labs(x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year")
```

### NAME IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

Each year's LAN size comes from its own [normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) with a shared standard deviation:

$$
X_{y} \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_y, \sigma = 2.5), \quad \mu_{1990} = 22, \; \mu_{1994} = 24, \; \mu_{1998} = 27
$$

The overlap depends on the distance between two means measured in standard deviations. The 1990 and 1998 means are $(27 - 22) / 2.5 = 2$ standard deviations apart, and the 1994 and 1998 means are only $(27 - 24) / 2.5 = 1.2$ apart. One way to put a number on that overlap is to pick a random office from each year and ask how often the "smaller" year wins:

$$
P(X_{1994} > X_{1998}) = \Phi\left(\frac{24 - 27}{2.5\sqrt{2}}\right) \approx 0.20
$$

So a 1994 office runs more workstations than a 1998 office about 20% of the time, while a 1990 office does so only about 8% of the time. Try moving the three means in `mean_nodes` closer together and the bars stack into a single colorful pile.

### CHANGE IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

So far the graph shows what we expect: each year is one pile, and the piles move right as LANs grow. Now we'll change the 1998 offices. Suppose the head offices kept growing to about 32 workstations, but the branch offices stayed small at about 21. We expect two 1998 piles, one far right and one back on top of the 1990 offices, with almost nothing near the 1998 average.

```{r}
#| label: change_data_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1990) # same seed as above
netware_split <- netware_offices |>
  mutate(
    split_mean = if_else(office <= 12, 32, 21), # 12 head offices, 12 branches
    nodes = if_else(year == "1998",
      round(rnorm(n(), mean = split_mean, sd = 1.5)), nodes),
    lan_size = if_else(nodes >= 25, "25 or more", "Under 25")) |>
  select(-split_mean)
netware_split |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(nodes), sd = sd(nodes),
    min = min(nodes), max = max(nodes))
```

The 1998 mean barely moved, to `r round(mean(netware_split$nodes[netware_split$year == "1998"]), 1)` workstations, but its standard deviation jumped to `r round(sd(netware_split$nodes[netware_split$year == "1998"]), 1)`. We'll redraw the same graph below with the same dashed lines.

```{r}
#| label: change_draw_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(data = netware_split,
    aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) +
  geom_bar() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(22, 24, 27),
    color = c("#69100A", "#A91E28", "#B3575A"),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Workstations", y = "Offices", fill = "Year")
```

The 1998 dashed line now sits in an empty stretch. None of the 1998 offices ran between 24 and 29 workstations. The `r sum(netware_split$year == "1998" & netware_split$nodes < 24)` branch offices pile up with the 1990 offices on the left, and the head offices sit alone on the right.

The mean says 1998 offices were a little bigger than 1994 offices, but the bars show that no 1998 office was typical. I've found this is the reason to look at the bars before comparing group means. A mean can't tell us when one group has split in two, but the overlapping colors can.


## Grammar


### CODE {.unnumbered .fm-step}

  -  Create labels with `labs()`

  -  Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  -  Map `nodes` to the `x` and `year` to `fill`

  -  Add the `geom_bar()` layer with `position = "identity"` (so the bars overlap instead of stacking) and `alpha = 0.5` (so the bars behind show through)

```{r}
#| label: code_graph_bar_ovrlp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true 
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_bar_ovrlp <- labs(
  title = "Novell NetWare",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "Workstations per office LAN in three years",
  x = "Workstations",
  y = "Offices",
  fill = "Year")
ggp2_bar_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_offices,
          aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) +
                geom_bar(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5)
ggp2_bar_ovrlp + 
  labs_bar_ovrlp
```

### GRAPH {.unnumbered .fm-step}

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_bar_ovrlp
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_bar_ovrlp <- labs(
  title = "Novell NetWare",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "Workstations per office LAN in three years",
  x = "Workstations",
  y = "Offices",
  fill = "Year")
ggp2_bar_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_offices,
          aes(x = nodes, fill = year)) +
                geom_bar(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5)
ggp2_bar_ovrlp + 
  labs_bar_ovrlp
```

## More info

  -  Overlapping bar graphs can also be built with `geom_col()`.

  -  `geom_bar()` has additional options for arranging overlapping bars. We can set the `position` argument to `"dodge"` or `"dodge2"`, depending on how we'd like the data displayed. 

### `geom_col()`

<br>

To build an overlapping bar graph with `geom_col()`, we need to create a column with the counts for `nodes` and `year` in the dataset. 

  -  Create the `netware_col` data:

```{r}
#| label: netware_col
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
netware_col <- netware_offices |>
    count(year, nodes, name = "Offices")
```


  -  Map the counts to the `y` axis, `nodes` to the `x` axis, and `year` to `fill`, and use the same `position` and `alpha` in `geom_col()`

```{r}
#| label: data_code_bar_netware_col
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_col_ovrlp <- labs(
  title = "Novell NetWare",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "built with 'geom_col()'",
  x = "Workstations",
  y = "Offices",
  fill = "Year")
ggp2_col_ovrlp <- ggplot(data = netware_col, 
    mapping = aes(y = Offices, 
        x = nodes, 
        fill = year)) + 
    geom_col(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5)
ggp2_col_ovrlp + 
    labs_col_ovrlp
```


Compare the two graphs below:

```{r}
#| label: compare_bar_col
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_bar_ovrlp + 
  labs_bar_ovrlp
ggp2_col_ovrlp + 
    labs_col_ovrlp
```

### `dodge`

<br>

::: {.column-margin}

- *`position = "dodge"` preserves the vertical position of a geom while adjusting the horizontal position*

- *`"dodge"` requires the grouping variable to be specified in the global or `⁠geom_`⁠ layer*

:::

::: {.fm-small}
We'll use the `lan_size` column, which splits offices into those with 25 workstations or more and those with fewer.
:::

```{r}
#| label: netware_dodge
#| eval: true
#| echo: true 
#| warning: false
#| message: false
count(netware_offices, lan_size, year)
```

  -  Create labels with `labs()`

  -  Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  -  Map `lan_size` to the `x` and `year` to `group` and `fill` 

  -  Inside the `geom_bar()` function, set `position` to `"dodge"`

```{r}
#| label: code_graph_dodge
#| eval: true
#| echo: true 
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_bar_dodge <- labs(
  title = "Novell NetWare",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "position = 'dodge'",
  x = "LAN size",
  y = "Offices",
  fill = "Year")
ggp2_bar_dodge <- ggplot(data = netware_offices,
                    aes(x = lan_size, 
                        group = year, 
                        fill = year)) +
                    geom_bar(
                        position = "dodge")
ggp2_bar_dodge +
  labs_bar_dodge
```

### `dodge2`

<br>

  -  Create labels with `labs()`

  -  Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  -  Map `lan_size` to `x` and `year` to `fill`

  -  Inside `geom_bar()`, set `position` to `"dodge2"`

::: {.column-margin}

- *`"dodge2"` works without a grouping variable in a layer*

- *`"dodge2"` works with bars and rectangles*  

- *`"dodge2"` is useful for arranging graphs with variable widths.*

:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_dodge2
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_bar_dodge2 <- labs(
  title = "Novell NetWare",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "position = 'dodge2'",
  x = "LAN size",
  y = "Offices",
  fill = "Year")
ggp2_bar_dodge2 <- ggplot(data = netware_offices,
                    aes(x = lan_size, 
                        fill = year)) +
                    geom_bar(
                        position = "dodge2")
ggp2_bar_dodge2 +
  labs_bar_dodge2
```

Compare the two graphs below:

```{r}
#| label: compare_bars
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_bar_dodge +
  labs_bar_dodge

ggp2_bar_dodge2 +
  labs_bar_dodge2
```
